tasks.short: Run the yearly merit and incentive round for office staff and check proposals against budget and CAO.

steps.what: Export salaries, grades, scale positions and appraisal scores from AFAS into Excel
Build merit matrix and budget per department
Send manager worksheets by mail, chase and collect proposals
Check proposals against budget, CAO scale maximums and gaps; settle exceptions
Approve, load pay changes in AFAS and produce employee letters

tasks.design: Replace the merit Excel workbook and mail round with a small app on the governed data platform: a nightly AFAS extract feeds a manager entry form with budget, scale ceiling and gap checks built in. The specialist sees one exception dashboard, approves, and the app writes pay mutations to AFAS through its API and generates letters from SharePoint templates.
tasks.previous_blocker: The round runs once a year with rules that change each time, so building an app was never worth it compared to a fresh Excel file.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes a small rule-driven app cheap enough to build and rebuild yearly, and AFAS exposes the data through its connectors.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding the matrix and handling managers who push past budget stays judgement; CAO staff on fixed scales need different rules than office staff.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the merit policy and saying no to a manager with a reason they accept.

ambition.what: Run a mid-year pay check per department instead of one yearly round, flagging people below band or with unexplained gaps.

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops chasing spreadsheets for weeks and spends the round on exceptions and on the merit policy itself, which they propose to the HR Director.

reach.task: Processing salary mutations in the month close
reach.learn: Which mutation fields and cut-off dates payroll needs so merit changes land in the right period.
How the merit budget ties to the yearly cost forecast.

evidence.claim: Rule checks and form workflows on AFAS data need no model at run time.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as fields that a merit app can read.
A pay system change can need works council consent under WOR 27(1)(c) unless the CAO settles it.

assumptions: Merit pay applies mainly to the 450 office staff; warehouse and transport staff follow CAO scale steps.
Appraisal scores are stored in AFAS.
unknowns: Whether Noordhaven has an incentive or bonus scheme beyond merit.
Whether the works council has consented to the current merit system.
research_questions: How many hours did the last merit round take, and how much was chasing and copying?
Does AFAS allow writing salary mutations through the API with an approval step?
How many proposals broke budget or scale rules last round?

tasks.short: Advise HRBPs and managers on employee complaints about job grade or salary.

steps.what: Receive complaint via HRBP or mail and log it
Gather job description, grade, pay history, peers and CAO rules

loop.output: Structured claim: which job, which grade asked, which peers named, which CAO article cited
loop.check: Extracted job and employee ids must match AFAS records; specialist confirms the claim summary
loop.stop: One pass plus one retry; on mismatch the specialist fills the claim by hand
loop.why_not_simpler: Complaints arrive as free text letters and mails, so the claim must be read before data can be pulled.

steps.what: Compare the job with evaluation factors and peers, form a view
Write advice to HRBP or manager

loop.input: Case file and the specialist's grading view with reasons
loop.output: Advice memo in the standard template
loop.check: Every figure in the memo is pulled from the case file, not generated; specialist edits and signs
loop.stop: One draft; if the view is missing reasons, no draft is made
loop.why_not_simpler: Advice must explain reasoning in plain Dutch for a specific case; a fixed template alone reads poorly.

steps.what: Discuss with HRBP, employee or complaints committee and follow up

tasks.design: Log complaints in a simple case register (SharePoint list or AFAS workflow) and auto-build a case file from AFAS and the job library, with a bounded model step that reads the complaint and one that drafts the advice memo. The judgement and the talk with the employee stay with the specialist; the same register later handles pay transparency information requests with their two-month deadline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Complaints are few, varied and written in free text, and the facts sit in AFAS, SharePoint and old Excel files, so nothing tied them together.
tasks.enabler_now: Models can reliably read a complaint letter into fields and draft a memo from given facts; the data join is cheap code.
tasks.still_hard: The grading view itself, peers who are not truly comparable, and complaints that are really about the manager. GDPR Art. 22 rules out a model deciding.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether two jobs are really equal and telling an employee no in a way that holds up.

ambition.what: A pay information request desk that answers employees' pay transparency requests within the legal two months.

tasks.altitude: Case prep shrinks to a check, so the specialist spends time on the view and the conversation and sees complaint patterns across jobs that point to grading fixes.

reach.learn: Which complaints reach the HRBP first and what they promise before C&B sees it.
How the gap figures by group are built, so complaint cases can be checked against them.

evidence.claim: Employees may request pay information and must get an answer within two months under the Dutch pay transparency bill.
Complaints are better treated as human-led, with the model as copilot.
GDPR Art. 22 bars a pay decision made solely by a model.

assumptions: There is an internal complaints procedure for grading, possibly from the CAO.
Job descriptions are stored on SharePoint.
unknowns: How many grade or salary complaints arrive per year.
Whether CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer complaints go to a sector committee rather than Noordhaven.
Whether the works council must be told about a model reading complaint letters.
research_questions: How many complaints in the last two years and how long did each take?
What share of case time is spent finding documents and figures?
Does the CAO prescribe a complaints procedure that limits the company's role?

tasks.short: Write job descriptions, grade jobs and maintain salary scales.

steps.what: Interview manager and job holder about tasks and responsibilities
Write job description in the SharePoint template

loop.input: Interview notes, old job description and related jobs from the library
loop.output: Job description in the template with the four factors filled
loop.check: Specialist and manager check it; template fields must all be filled
loop.stop: Up to two redrafts on comments; then the specialist edits by hand
loop.why_not_simpler: Notes are free text; turning them into a consistent description needs language work.

steps.what: Score the job on evaluation factors and propose a grade

loop.input: Job description and factor definitions with reference jobs
loop.output: Score per factor with reasons and the nearest reference jobs
loop.check: Specialist compares with reference jobs; a score more than one level off a near reference is flagged
loop.stop: One pass per factor; low confidence or conflict goes to the specialist unscored
loop.why_not_simpler: Factor scoring means reading a description against definitions; rules cannot read prose.

steps.what: Update salary scales from CAO tables and market data
Get approval and record job, grade and scale in AFAS

tasks.design: Build a job library on the governed platform with SharePoint templates: a bounded model step drafts the description and a per-factor score with reasons, the specialist decides, and an AFAS workflow records the approved job scheme and band. Salary scales become a versioned table fed from CAO tables, replacing the Excel copies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Job descriptions were free text and grading relied on the specialist's reading; no tool could draft or score them.
tasks.enabler_now: Models now draft descriptions and score factors well enough to start from, and AFAS Profit 8 has fields for job schemes ready for pay transparency.
tasks.still_hard: Scores are about 70% right, so every grade needs a real check; CAO jobs stay in the CAO system now being redone by the sector. A grade recommendation tool may be high-risk under the AI Act from December 2027.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing what a job really involves on the floor and defending the grade to the manager and works council.

ambition.what: A complete job architecture with a four-factor evaluation for every office job, ready for the 2027 pay transparency report.

tasks.altitude: The specialist moves from grading jobs one by one to owning the job architecture, deciding which roles need regrading and which drift does not count.

reach.task: Writing vacancy texts and quoting salary bands
reach.learn: How bands are shown before negotiation and why salary history is no longer asked.

reach.task: Maintaining AFAS job and organisation data
reach.learn: How job schemes are coded so reports group jobs correctly.

evidence.claim: A UK university pilot graded job descriptions per HERA factor with ChatGPT at over 70% agreement with experts.
AFAS Profit 8 stores job schemes and categories as preparation for pay transparency.
Job evaluation must use skills, responsibilities, effort and working conditions, and the works council consents to the system.
Grade or pay recommendations can be high-risk under AI Act Annex III 4(b) from 2 December 2027.
CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer parties are regrading the sector's jobs.

assumptions: Office jobs use an in-house or purchased evaluation method; CAO jobs use the CAO grid.
Job descriptions are Word files on SharePoint.
unknowns: Which job evaluation method Noordhaven uses for office jobs.
How many distinct jobs exist and how many lack a current description.
When the sector regrading of CAO jobs is expected.
research_questions: On 20 recently graded jobs, how often does the model's factor score match the specialist's?
How many hours does one job description and grade take today?
Will the works council consent to a model-drafted grade with human decision?

tasks.short: Cost CAO proposals and pay scenarios from payroll data for negotiators and Finance.

steps.what: Extract headcount, pay, hours, allowances and agency hours
Clean and reconcile the data with the general ledger
Model scenarios: wage rise, allowances, pension premium, flex mix
Write findings for HR and Finance Directors and negotiators

loop.input: Scenario tables and the specialist's key points
loop.output: Memo and slides with tables generated from the model
loop.check: All numbers come from the scenario tables by code; specialist reviews wording
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; then manual
loop.why_not_simpler: Tables can be generated by code, but the short narrative for directors needs writing.

tasks.design: Replace the costing workbooks with a scheduled extract of AFAS payroll and agency portal hours on the governed data platform, reconciled to the ledger, plus a scenario calculator where the specialist sets wage, allowance and pension parameters. A Power BI page shows results and a bounded model step drafts the memo around code-generated tables.
tasks.previous_blocker: Costing happens a few times a year with new proposals each round, and agency data came in different files, so Excel stayed the cheapest tool.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes a reusable extract and scenario calculator quick to build; the AFAS nightly extract for Power BI already exists.
tasks.still_hard: Agency data quality, pension changes with Pensioenfonds Vervoer's new scheme, and knowing what the other side will accept.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which scenario matters at the table and explaining cost trade-offs to negotiators.

ambition.what: Cost every counter-proposal during CAO talks the same day instead of after a week.

tasks.altitude: The specialist becomes the live costing partner in negotiations, with the right to set scenario assumptions with the controller.

reach.task: Personnel cost reconciliation to the ledger
reach.learn: Which ledger accounts hold wages, allowances and agency costs.
How CAO outcomes flow into the yearly forecast.

evidence.claim: CAO costing is deterministic calculation on payroll data.
Pensioenfonds Vervoer expects its new scheme on 1 January 2027, changing pension premiums.
Agency workers count in pay transparency and agencies supply their pay data.

assumptions: Noordhaven negotiates its own warehouse CAO and supports the sector CAO costing.
unknowns: Whether Noordhaven's drivers are in Pensioenfonds Vervoer.
Whether the three agencies give exports in a stable format.
Who negotiates the warehouse CAO for the company.
research_questions: How long did costing the last CAO proposal take, and how many rounds were there?
Can the AFAS extract give allowances and overtime per employee per month?
Do the controller's ledger totals match the payroll extract within 1%?

role.altitude: From grading jobs and running pay rounds by hand to owning the job architecture and the evidence behind every pay difference, ready for the pay transparency report over 2027.
reach: Pay gap reporting with the People Analytics and HRIS Analyst
Salary mutations and cut-offs with the Payroll Specialist
Salary bands in vacancies with Recruiters
skills_to_grow: Four-factor job evaluation and its defence to the works council
Reviewing model-drafted grades and logging oversight under the AI Act
Specifying rules for small apps on the data platform
Pay gap analysis and explaining gaps
role.ambitious_version: Every job at Noordhaven has a current description, a four-factor grade and a band in AFAS; gaps by group are checked each quarter; pay requests are answered within two months; and CAO counter-proposals are costed the same day.
